memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You must not offer to the LORD an animal whose testicles are
bruised, crushed, torn or cut. You must not do this in your own land,
and you must not accept such animals from the hand of a foreigner and
offer them as the food of your God. They will not be accepted on your
behalf, because they are deformed and defective'" - Lev 22:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God anticipates a clever workaround here. If an Israelite could not
offer a damaged animal from his own flock, perhaps he could buy one
cheaply from a foreign trader and offer that instead. Technically it
was not his own. Technically he had not damaged it.

God closes that door too. The standard did not change depending on
where the animal came from.

We are remarkably good at this kind of reasoning. We find the technical
loophole that keeps the letter of the rule while emptying it of
meaning. Jesus confronted exactly this in the religious leaders of His
day - they tithed their garden herbs meticulously while neglecting
justice, mercy and faithfulness (Matt 23:23).

Dear friend, God is not impressed by technicalities. He looks at the
heart behind the arrangement. A conscience that is always searching for
the minimum acceptable standard has already drifted from love.

The good news is that Christ has freed us from this exhausting
loophole-hunting. We are not trying to do the least that God will
accept. We are responding to a love that gave everything. When we
truly grasp grace, we stop asking how little we can get away with.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I looking for a loophole instead of obeying honestly?
2. Do I ask "what is the minimum?" or "what would honour God?"
3. How does grace free me from technical religion?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You see straight through my clever excuses. Give me a heart that
wants to honour You, not one that looks for the smallest acceptable
offering. Amen.
